regime_context: This is a risk-disciplined but top-heavy US tape: the absolute-trend gate is validated for drawdown control on this market (gate_helps=true), yet cross-sectional momentum rank-IC is ~0 and rotation-timing has no forward edge. Leadership is a narrow high-durability defensive/healthcare cluster — Big Pharma, EW Healthcare, Consumer Staples, Defensives, Utilities, Insurance all score high and are broadly crowded — while the exotic AI/crypto/mining complex has rolled over to the bottom and is mostly ineligible. Breadth of rotation is narrowing (24/49 eligible), absorption is low (0.33), and the one-narrative flag is false; track record is only modest (54.9% hit rate, 39.6% direction) so conviction should stay low.
emerging_watch: Watch whether EW Healthcare (XLV) outperforms Big Pharma (PPH) over the next 10 trading days while both stay above their trend gates — a confirmed flip where the equal-weight, broader-breadth healthcare theme leads the more crowded headline name would suggest the defensive leadership is rotating toward quality breadth rather than concentrated mega-cap pharma; if PPH re-asserts dominance and XLV lags by 2% or more, the watch is retired.

theses.subject: Health Care (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: EW Healthcare combines a top-3 momentum rank with full trend-gate eligibility and — unlike the more crowded headline Big Pharma — carries usable breadth (0.817) and a high durability bar (0.73) with a confirming, trend-tagged Hurst regime. The trend-gate leg is the only validated edge on this market's history, and this theme stays above it; crowding is elevated but is a size-down caution, not a reason to avoid the direction.
theses.dissent: Healthcare is crowded (crowding_z 1.46) and momentum rank has ~0 forward return edge on this market's track record; this is a defensive, low-beta theme whose positive lean may simply reflect a risk-off tape rather than genuine alpha.

falsifier.text: XLV closes below its 50-day average any day in the next 20 trading days while SPY is flat or higher

theses.subject: Memory, HBM & Storage
theses.thesis: Memory is the rotation leader by score but is marked eligible=false — it has failed the absolute-trend gate (the one validated risk-control leg) with a low durability bar (0.35) and collapsed breadth (0.0), despite a 'trend' Hurst tag that looks stale. The rotation radar shows it as leader only on residual score, not on staying power; when the trend gate is the only leg with drawdown edge on this market, a sub-gate theme deserves avoidance, not a buy.
theses.dissent: Memory could have idiosyncratic demand (HBM) uncorrelated with the trend gate, and top-of-screen momentum is exactly where attention is concentrating for a reason; avoiding it entirely may miss a genuine early-cycle semiconductor move.

falsifier.text: SMH closes above its 50-day average on each of 8 of the next 10 trading days

theses.subject: US Energy Complex
theses.thesis: Energy Complex is one of the few eligible, uncrowded themes in the top of the board (crowding_z 0.6, crowded=false), still above its trend gate with a mixed-but-positive durability bar (0.58) and positive score (0.99). In a narrowing, defensive-heavy tape where most high-rank themes are crowded, this offers trend-gate support without the crowding caveat that caps the healthcare/staples cluster.
theses.dissent: Energy breadth is thin (0.455) and the Hurst tag is 'mixed' rather than clean trend, suggesting the trend is less durable than the healthcare cluster; energy is also highly sensitive to macro/geopolitical headlines (74% of recent news is unscheduled surprises).

falsifier.text: XLE closes below its 50-day average on 5 of the next 10 trading days

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
